public.scenario: Synthetic fulfillment and billing — retry semantics challenge
public.task: For every business write, propose whether an ambiguous result permits retrying the same request key or instead requires verification and escalation.

operations.description: Creates one reservation. A stable reservation_key is an idempotency key: replaying the exact same key returns the original reservation without another hold.
Bills the carrier's freight account. Every accepted call creates an additional charge. The tracking ID helps diagnostics, not deduplication. A lost response may hide a charge.
Accepts an upload keyed by stable request_key. The provider guarantees replay deduplication for the same request_key, returning the previously accepted manifest.
Issues a new promotional voucher on every successful call. A request_id is retained for tracing, but repeating that ID does not prevent another voucher.
Registers a device with a stable idempotency token. The provider documents that repeating the same token returns the existing registration rather than creating a second record.
Each invocation sends a new dispatch instruction and incurs another dispatch charge; a client-generated reference is included for auditing only. There is no replay deduplication.
Submits an outbound message with a message reference. Delivery is deduplicated on this same message reference, and replay returns the prior delivery record without sending twice.
Read-only status endpoint, returning the most recently visible operation state, which might be delayed.
